candidate.title: 4-C
candidate.scope: The middle poster row labelled 4-C / Chromatin conformation capture circular (4-C), at schematic scope. The matched collection heading identifies 4C, also called 4C-seq, as the sequencing-associated assay discussed here; these are aliases in this context, not separate target workflows. The supplied crop also shows NG Capture-C above and UMI-4C below, and a clipped earlier row at its top edge; those are independent neighboring rows, not alternatives or branches of the assigned 4-C target. No material transfer, pooling or historical-development edge connects them to this row. Extract only the central route from chromatin to DNA. The combined self-circularization/reverse-PCR caption is decomposed at the visibly circular intermediate. Sequencing is a text-supported readout interface and is not invented as a drawn operation. This is not a full experimental protocol or an assertion that all 4C implementations share identical chemistry.

unknowns.question: The blue crosslinked protein is drawn at Ligation and absent at Restriction digest. Where does crosslink reversal/protein removal occur in the implementation intended by this schematic? The supplied abstracts and catalogue do not place it. A relevant primary methods passage would be needed to add that local operation; its omission does not prevent reading the depicted ligation-to-redigestion route. Targeted reads of the Zhao publisher page and the Cai PMC page returned browser challenge pages, so no primary full-text reaction order was verified.

What do the yellow rectangle (from ligation onward), magenta rectangle on the circle and adjacent teal arrows encode? The reverse-PCR caption establishes the circular-template amplification interface, but a legend or intended primary figure would be needed to assign particular primer-binding sites, restriction sites or end modifications. No barcode, adaptor or chemical identity is inferred from these unlabelled symbols.
